cleared.check: Task 1, jump pairs 9042/9048 (unlockCallback CALL, PoolManager.sol:110) and 15088/15094 (balanceOf STATICCALL, Currency.sol:94). Sides: 9048 falls through to 9049 with the result left at its default 0 and skips the decoding of the returned bytes; 15094 falls through to 15095 and returns the default 0 balance without decoding. Condition for the untaken side: the success word is zero at 9048 (or 15094) while it was nonzero at 9042 (or 15088).
cleared.result: Unreachable on every network for any value a CALL or STATICCALL can push. The disassembly of the build reads CALL, SWAP1, DUP2, ISZERO, PUSH2 0x24c2, JUMPI at 9035-9042 and PUSH0, SWAP2, PUSH2 0x241a, JUMPI at 9043-9048, and STATICCALL, SWAP1, DUP2, ISZERO, PUSH2 0x24c2, JUMPI, PUSH0, SWAP2, PUSH2 0x3afa, JUMPI at 15081-15094. Both JUMPIs of a pair test the same stack word: the first leaves through 0x24c2 (9410: RETURNDATACOPY of all return data and REVERT) when the word is zero, the second runs only when it is nonzero and then jumps. No network can make one word both zero and nonzero, so a CALL that returns 2, or any other nonzero word, still takes the decode side. The decode side checks return data size (9263-9272 for unlockCallback, 15104-15108 for balanceOf, both require at least 32 bytes) and reverts otherwise. callsem.py, rerun this session on all 21 networks, returned 50 of 50 specified words, including the success flags of calls that revert, fail a static write or carry value.

cleared.check: Task 1, pc 15021 (Currency.sol:91-92). Sides: taken goes to the balanceOf STATICCALL at 15026, fallthrough runs SELFBALANCE at 15023. Condition for the untaken side: the currency word masked to 160 bits is zero inside balanceOfSelf.
cleared.result: Unreachable on all 21 networks. balanceOfSelf has two callers, sync (PoolManager.sol:281-285) and _settle (PoolManager.sol:353-359), and each tests isAddressZero on the same currency value first and takes another branch for address(0). The condition is AND and JUMPI on a value from calldata or transient storage; it reads no environment opcode, so no chain property enters. SELFBALANCE stays dead code, and no network difference in SELFBALANCE (for example a native balance mirrored elsewhere, F-008 on Polygon or the USDC faces on Arc) can reach the settlement arithmetic through it.

cleared.check: Task 1, pc 16370 (Hooks.sol:137). Sides: fallthrough computes bytes4(data) from a hook calldata shorter than 4 bytes; taken uses the first 4 bytes. Condition: mload(data) < 4.
cleared.result: Unreachable on all 21 networks. data is always an abi.encodeCall of an IHooks selector with at least one argument (Hooks.sol:180, 190, 202, 204, 225, 237, 256, 300, 323, 333), so its length is at least 36 bytes. The length is written by the compiler's encoder in memory and does not depend on any opcode result outside MLOAD and LT, which the opcode battery covers.

cleared.check: Task 1, ABI decoder bounds at pcs 1378, 2396, 3087, 5298, 10926 and 11947. Sides: revert to 816 when calldata is shorter than the head of a second static struct. Condition: CALLDATASIZE minus 4 is less than the head of the second struct while an earlier JUMPI of the same function (for example 1327 before 1378) passed with a larger bound.
cleared.result: Unreachable on all 21 networks. Both tests compare CALLDATASIZE, a single value per frame, against two constants, and the earlier test uses the larger one. A network cannot return two CALLDATASIZE values in one frame. pmdiff4 (malformed calldata on a third of 10,773 calls) matched the reference on all 21 networks in cycle 12.

cleared.check: Task 1, Panic 0x41 at pcs 5583, 11761, 11789, 11817 and 19089. Sides: Panic 0x41 when a memory struct allocation moves the free memory pointer above 2^64 - 1 or below its old value. Condition: the free memory pointer exceeds about 2^64 before the allocation. The one input from outside that moves the pointer before these allocations is hook return data, because callHook advances the pointer by returndatasize rounded up plus 32 (Hooks.sol:142-148).
cleared.result: Unreachable on all 21 networks. Reaching 2^64 needs return data of about 2^64 bytes, which no transaction gas cap allows: the largest simulated call gas any endpoint grants is about 150 million on Monad (OPCODES.md check 2), while 2^64 bytes of memory cost far more than 2^100 gas under the quadratic rule. The edge script set B (beforeInitialize returning 31, 32, 33, 4,096, 65,536, 262,144 and 1,048,576 bytes; beforeSwap returning 95, 96, 97 and 65,536 bytes) gave the reference interpreter's answer on Ethereum, Arbitrum One, BNB Smart Chain, Monad, Tempo and HyperEVM in the earlier attempt, and again this session on Arbitrum One, Monad and Tempo (39 of 39 scripts each). 31 bytes and 95 or 97 bytes revert with InvalidHookResponse (0x1e048e1d), and every other length passes on to the swap allocations without a Panic.

cleared.check: Task 1, pc 12293. Sides: Panic 0x11 of a checked uint256 addition to an ERC-6909 balance. Condition: a receiver balance plus amount reaches 2^256. The jumpmap cites ERC6909.sol:147, 162 and 199, which do not exist in the 90 line file; the additions are at ERC6909.sol:28 (transfer), 43 (transferFrom) and 80 (_mint).
cleared.result: No network property is involved. Supply of an id grows only by mint, whose amount passes toInt128 (SafeCast.sol:56-57, below 2^127) and must be paid through the delta of the same currency (PoolManager.sol:322-329). Overflow needs about 2^129 mints of one id, and transfers only move existing supply. The arithmetic is ADD and GT, which the battery covers on all 21 networks.

cleared.check: Task 1, the revert guards of the math: 16750 (InvalidTick, TickMath.sol:70), 17660, 17698, 19752, 19780, 20339, 20353 (toInt256, SafeCast.sol:50), 19792 (checked int256 subtraction, Pool.sol:375), 18728 and 23677 (mulmod by liquidity 0, FullMath.sol:112), 20420 and 20741 (InvalidPriceOrLiquidity, SqrtPriceMath.sol:135-143 and 164-172), 21212 and 23521 (require(x > 0) of the bit scans, BitMath.sol:32 and 13), 22353, 22468, 22618, 22741, 22912 (require(denominator > prod1) of constant-denominator copies of mulDiv, FullMath.sol:30), 23248 and 23430 (InvalidPrice, SqrtPriceMath.sol:197-202), 23695 (require(++result > 0), FullMath.sol:113), 23781 (PriceOverflow, SqrtPriceMath.sol:59-69) and 23994 (toUint160, SqrtPriceMath.sol:71). The untaken side of each is a revert.
cleared.result: Unreachable on all 21 networks under specified opcode results, and a revert in any case. Rechecked by hand: getSqrtPriceAtTick receives ticks bounded by checkTicks (Pool.sol:94-98) or by the clamp at Pool.sol:351-356; a step amount is at most about 2^192 (liquidity below 2^128 times a price below 2^160, over prices of at least 2^32), so the int256 casts and the loop sum stay below 2^255; computeSwapStep with liquidity 0 computes a zero amount to the target and always reaches it (SwapMath.sol:63-99), so getNextSqrtPriceFrom* never sees liquidity 0, and those functions test liquidity before the mulmod in any case; an exact output step that stops short has amount times price below liquidity times 2^96 (SqrtPriceMath.sol:59-71), so neither PriceOverflow nor the toUint160 cast can fire. Each condition is a relation among ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MULMOD, SHL, SHR, LT, GT, SLT, SGT, ISZERO and AND results, so a network could make one true only by returning a word the specification does not give. The 185,529 battery vectors and the 2,000 or so scripts on the build show no such word on any of the 21 networks, and these sides would only turn a success into a revert, which takes no funds.

cleared.check: Task 1, the payout-affecting untaken sides: 20776 with 20942, 20963 and 20971 (amount above type(uint160).max in the subtract branch of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount1RoundingDown, SqrtPriceMath.sol:102-106), 22746 (prod1 == 0 inside the mulDiv(amount, Q96, liquidity) copy, FullMath.sol:33), 20840 (NotEnoughLiquidity, SqrtPriceMath.sol:109-114), 23217 and 23399 (the price swap of getAmount0Delta, SqrtPriceMath.sol:194) and 23705 (amount == 0 in the output copy of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp, SqrtPriceMath.sol:37).
cleared.result: None of these sides depends on a network property. 23217 and 23399: every call passes the lower price first (SwapMath.sol:67, 86, 90, 101; Pool.sol:212-232), and with prices in order the swap is not needed; if it ran, the result would be the same amount. 22746: the copy runs only for amount at least 2^160, and 2^160 times 2^96 is 2^256, so prod1 is at least 1. 23705: an exact output step that stops short passes amountRemaining, which is positive inside the loop (Pool.sol:344). 20840: the output is below the output to the target, so the quotient is below the price difference. 20776 can in principle be reached: an exact output of more than 2^160 units of currency1 that stops short of its target needs liquidity above about 2^96 over most of the price range and a pool holding more than 2^160 units of currency1, which only a token with a supply above 2^160 allows, that is a token its author made for it (one line token hazard, actor pool-creator, no loss: the branch computes FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp, which v4math.py checks on 200,000 inputs and the battery checks per opcode).

cleared.check: Task 2, transient storage cleared at the end of the transaction and rolled back on revert (Lock.sol:12-26, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol, CurrencyDelta.sol:28-41, CurrencyReserves.sol:28-31).
cleared.result: The source needs end-of-transaction clearing for two slots only. unlock always ends by writing false to the lock slot (PoolManager.sol:113) or reverts, and it reverts unless NonzeroDeltaCount is zero (PoolManager.sol:112). _accountDelta increments the count only when a delta goes from zero to nonzero and decrements it only when a nonzero delta returns to zero (PoolManager.sol:368-378), so a zero count means every delta slot is zero. What outlives a completed unlock is the synced currency and reserves, which is F-071 for a shared transaction. The property whose failure would hand funds to an ordinary account is rollback on revert: a lock flag or a credit written in a frame that reverts must disappear. callsem.py, rerun this session, gave the specified words for the transient write after a reverted write, a static write, a nested write and two failures on all 21 networks. The special contexts were cleared in earlier cycles and are not repeated: Tempo type 0x76 batches, HyperEVM system transactions, Nitro retryables and deposits, OP Stack deposits, MegaETH mini-blocks, Monad, Polygon and BNB Smart Chain parallel execution with re-execution (bor resets transient storage per transaction and per re-execution; Monad drops a failed frame's copy, state3/state.cpp 126-181), Celo fee debit and credit calls and ERC-4337 or EIP-7702 bundles (state/cleared.json). Within one shared transaction the lock and the deltas cannot pass from one party to the next for the reason above.

cleared.check: Task 2, msg.value seen once per call frame (PoolManager.sol:300-307, 354).
cleared.result: _settle reads CALLVALUE once per settle or settleFor call and credits it once. The source contains no DELEGATECALL (no match for delegatecall in src/ outside comments), so no frame of the PoolManager runs twice with one value. A contract that delegatecalls into the PoolManager code runs it on its own storage and transient storage, which holds no pool funds. callsem.py confirms on all 21 networks that a call with value moves exactly that many wei or none. Network specifics were cleared before: Tempo has no native asset, the BNB Smart Chain system address runs a call with a stated value that moves no balance (F-058, governance), and the two faces of the native asset on Celo, Polygon and Arc are covered by F-023, F-008 and F-032.

cleared.check: Task 2, the gas forwarding rule around the five outgoing calls: the unlock callback (PoolManager.sol:110), the native payout and the token transfer (Currency.sol:48, 73), the balanceOf read (Currency.sol:94) and the hook call (Hooks.sol:134).
cleared.result: Every one of them forwards all gas and reverts the PoolManager frame when the callee fails: 9042 and 15088 jump to the revert at 9410, Currency.sol:51-52 and 82-86 and Hooks.sol:137 call bubbleUpAndRevertWith. No call site continues after a failed call or reads a gas-dependent value. A network that forwards a different share (MegaETH forwards 98/100, OPCODES.md cycle 13) changes only whether the remaining frame can pay for its revert, and both outcomes are a revert. A recipient of a native payout that fails for lack of gas fails the caller's own take.

cleared.check: Task 2, return data of a call to an address with no code or to a precompile or system contract named as currency, hook or recipient. Script set A of edges.py ran sync, the synced words, settle, sync, a zero take and settle, and initialize where the address has valid hook bits, for every special address of the network: precompiles 0x01 to 0x11 and 0x100, the OP Stack predeploys on the nine OP Stack networks, and the per network lists of ASSUMPTIONS.md and networks.json (Celo 0xfd and 0x471E, Nitro 0x64 to 0xc8, Polygon 0x1000 to 0x1010, BNB 0x1000 to 0x2002, Avalanche 0x0100.., 0x0200.., Monad 0x1000 and 0x1001, MegaETH 0x6342..01, Tempo 0x20C0, 0x403C, 0xfeEC, Arc 0x3600, 0x1800..05, 0x1800..09, HyperEVM 0x800 to 0x813 and 0x2222..22).
cleared.result: Run this session on all 21 networks, 476 scripts, every one equal to the earlier attempt except the HyperEVM L1 block number word. sync succeeds only where the callee returns at least 32 bytes: sha256 (0x02), ripemd160 (0x03) and identity (0x04) on every network, WETH9 at 0x4200..06 on the OP Stack chains, the CELO token, Polygon 0x1010, Tempo 0x20C0.., Arc USDC 0x3600.. and HyperEVM 0x809. In every case the settle that follows in the same transaction credits 0, because the returned word does not change inside the transaction. A zero take of these addresses fails with ERC20TransferFailed (0x90bfb865) where the returned word is not 1, and succeeds where the callee has no code or is a real token. The precompiles that charge for their input (0x05 to 0x11 and several system contracts) consume the forwarded gas, and the whole script fails, which is the caller's own loss. initialize succeeds with the codeless hook 0x100, and with 0x10 on Avalanche and HyperEVM, because those flag combinations call no hook at initialize. A credit in a currency id such as 0x02 or 0x809 is a claim on a balance that no other user holds, so it takes nothing from anyone.

cleared.check: HyperEVM 0x809 as currency: the precompile ignores its input and returns the L1 block number (0x49885a18 in the earlier run, 0x49887a1e this session).
cleared.result: sync(0x809) stores the block number as reserves and the settle in the same transaction credits 0. If the word could change between two calls in one transaction, the difference would be booked as a payment in currency 0x809, which no pool or claim holder owns, so no user funds are reachable through it. take of 0x809 always fails because the word is not 1.

Events are emitted before the after-hooks so that logs appear in call order. No decision in src/ reads a log, so an ordering difference on any network would affect indexers only. MegaETH and HyperEVM receipts were compared with a second execution in cycles 10 and 11.

cleared.check: Task 2, dirty upper bits that assembly in src/ cleans or assumes clean: masks in Currency.sol:61, CurrencyDelta.sol:12-13, CurrencyReserves.sol:29, CustomRevert.sol:25, 43, 64-65, 75-76, 97-100, 115, SqrtPriceMath.sol:62, 110, 137-138, 166-167, 198, 217, SwapMath.sol:31-33, LiquidityMath.sol:12 and the signextend calls of TickBitmap.sol:20-21, 38, 54-55 and CustomRevert.sol:34, 53-54; and the places that use a word unmasked: Lock.isUnlocked (Lock.sol:25), ParseBytes (ParseBytes.sol:12, 19, 26) and Position.calculatePositionKey (Position.sol:54-66).
cleared.result: No case depends on a network. Values from calldata pass the ABI decoder, which rejects dirty high bits (set C3, sync of an address word with bits above 160 set, reverts on the reference and on the six networks of set C). The lock slot is only ever written with true or false (Lock.sol:13, 19). ParseBytes returns full words that the compiler cleans to bytes4, uint24 or int256 where they are used, and each read follows a length check (Hooks.sol:152, 166, 259). In the position key the upper bytes of each mstore are overwritten by the next store or lie outside the hashed range [0x0c, 0x46), so dirty ticks or owner bits cannot change the key. AND, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL and SHR are in the battery on all 21 networks.

cleared.check: Task 3, the assembly that writes memory without moving the free memory pointer: CustomRevert (exits at once), Hooks.callHook (allocates from returndatasize, Hooks.sol:140-149), Currency.transfer (calldata at the free pointer, output to 0..32, then zeroes 0x60 bytes, Currency.sol:55-80), Extsload and Exttload (do-while loops, Extsload.sol:18-63, Exttload.sol:18-38), ParseBytes and Position.calculatePositionKey. Edge inputs: hook return data of 31 to 1,048,576 bytes, a reverting hook with 0, 1, 31, 32, 33 and 32,768 bytes of data, extsload(start, n) for n = 0, 1, 2, 2^251, 2^251 + 1, 2^251 + 2, 2^256 - 2 and 2^256 - 1, the array forms with length words 0, 1, 2^251, 2^251 + 1, 2^64 - 1 and 2^64, and a dirty address word in sync.
cleared.result: Each block assumes only that memory above the free pointer is scratch it may overwrite and that RETURNDATASIZE gives the length the callee returned. Currency.transfer trusts mload(0) only when return data is longer than 31 bytes and fails on 1 to 31 bytes; Yul evaluates the call before the or() term, which the bytecode does. The extsload loops run once even for n = 0 and then return the 64 byte header. For n = 2^256 - 1 the shifted length wraps and the function returns 32 bytes, for n = 2^256 - 2 it returns 0 bytes, and 2^251 returns a header with length 2^251 and no elements; all are view calls that cannot move funds. The array forms with a length of 2^64 or 2^251 are refused by the ABI decoder. The wrapped error for a reverting hook grows by 32 bytes per word of data, 228 bytes for empty data. All 39 scripts gave the reference interpreter's bytes on Ethereum, Arbitrum One, BNB Smart Chain, Monad, Tempo and HyperEVM in the earlier attempt, and again this session on Arbitrum One (Nitro, go-ethereum fork), Monad (C++ interpreter) and Tempo (evm2).

leads.question: Do mined PoolManager transactions on Tempo, Arc, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche and the Nitro chains contain an unlock frame that reverted followed by a later unlock that completed, and does the later frame see a locked manager and zero deltas?
leads.why: Rollback of transient storage on revert is the one EVM property whose failure would give an ordinary account a leaked unlock flag or credit. It is tested by simulated calls on all 21 networks and by mined transactions only on MegaETH, HyperEVM, Polygon and Monad.
